stemMd: What volume of 0.20 mol/L sodium hydroxide exactly neutralises 30 mL of 0.10 mol/L hydrochloric acid?
explanationMd: The acid supplies 0.030 times 0.10 = 0.003 mol H+. The one-to-one reaction needs 0.003 mol hydroxide, requiring 0.003/0.20 = 0.015 L, or 15 mL.

distractorRationale.b: Equal volumes would require equal concentrations.
distractorRationale.a: This loses a factor of five in the mole balance.
